4.label: Exceeds Standard
4.description: Demonstrates deep understanding; solves complex, multi-step problems accurately; justifies reasoning with mathematical precision.

3.label: Meets Standard
3.description: Consistently applies grade-level concepts correctly with minor errors; meets all CCSS expectations.

2.label: Approaching Standard
2.description: Partially applies concepts; makes procedural errors; inconsistent accuracy across question types.

1.label: Below Standard
1.description: Limited or no grasp of grade-level concepts; significant errors; unable to complete standard tasks independently.

standards.description: Understand the concept of a ratio and use ratio language to describe a ratio relationship between two quantities.

levels.4: Correctly describes ratios using part-to-part and part-to-whole language in multiple contexts; distinguishes ratio from fraction; explains in context.
levels.3: Correctly identifies and describes ratio relationships using ratio language with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Identifies a ratio but uses imprecise language or confuses part-to-part with part-to-whole.
levels.1: Cannot correctly identify or describe ratio relationships.

standards.description: Understand the concept of a unit rate a/b associated with a ratio a:b with b ≠ 0; use rate language in the context of a ratio relationship.

levels.4: Finds and interprets unit rates in varied contexts; explains the meaning of the unit rate; compares rates across problems.
levels.3: Correctly calculates unit rates and uses rate language accurately with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Calculates a rate but does not simplify to a unit rate or confuses rate language.
levels.1: Cannot calculate or interpret unit rates.

standards.description: Use ratio and rate reasoning to solve real-world and mathematical problems (tables, tape diagrams, double number lines, equations, percent, unit conversion).

levels.4: Uses multiple representations (table, double number line, equation) to solve ratio/rate problems; solves complex percent and conversion problems; justifies solutions.
levels.3: Correctly solves ratio and rate problems using at least one appropriate representation with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Solves simple ratio problems but makes errors with percent, unit conversion, or multi-step problems.
levels.1: Cannot apply ratio or rate reasoning to solve problems.

standards.description: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100; solve problems involving finding the whole, given a part and the percent.

levels.4: Finds percent of a quantity, the whole from a part and percent, and the percent given part and whole; applies in multi-step real-world problems.
levels.3: Correctly finds percent of a quantity and solves for the whole given part and percent with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Finds percent of a quantity correctly but struggles to find the whole or the percent itself.
levels.1: Cannot apply percent concepts to solve problems.

standards.description: Interpret and compute quotients of fractions; solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions.

levels.4: Divides fractions by fractions fluently; interprets the quotient in context; creates and solves original word problems; uses visual models to explain.
levels.3: Correctly divides fractions by fractions using keep-change-flip and solves related word problems with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Applies the division procedure but makes errors with mixed numbers or cannot interpret the quotient in context.
levels.1: Cannot divide fractions by fractions or interpret fraction division.

standards.description: Fluently divide multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm.

levels.4: Applies the standard algorithm fluently; zero errors; explains each step; identifies and corrects errors in others' work.
levels.3: Correctly divides multi-digit numbers using the standard algorithm with ≤1 computational error.
levels.2: Uses the algorithm but makes systematic errors with two-digit divisors or remainders.
levels.1: Cannot apply the standard long division algorithm correctly.

standards.description: Fluently add, subtract, multiply, and divide multi-digit decimals using the standard algorithm for each operation.

levels.4: Performs all four decimal operations fluently and accurately; explains the role of place value alignment; zero errors.
levels.3: Correctly performs multi-digit decimal operations with ≤1 computational error.
levels.2: Adds and subtracts decimals correctly; makes errors multiplying or dividing decimals (misplaces decimal point).
levels.1: Cannot reliably perform multi-digit decimal operations.

standards.description: Find the greatest common factor (GCF) of two whole numbers ≤100 and the least common multiple (LCM) of two whole numbers ≤12; use the distributive property to express a sum as a product.

levels.4: Finds GCF and LCM accurately; uses the distributive property to factor and expand expressions; applies GCF/LCM in context problems.
levels.3: Correctly finds GCF and LCM and applies the distributive property with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Finds GCF or LCM correctly but not both; limited application of distributive property.
levels.1: Cannot reliably find GCF or LCM.

standards.description: Understand that positive and negative numbers describe quantities having opposite directions or values; use positive and negative numbers in real-world contexts.

levels.4: Accurately interprets positive and negative numbers in diverse real-world contexts; explains what zero means in each context; compares signed quantities.
levels.3: Correctly interprets and uses positive and negative numbers in real-world contexts with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Identifies positive and negative in simple contexts (temperature, money) but struggles with less familiar applications.
levels.1: Cannot interpret or use positive and negative numbers in context.

standards.description: Understand a rational number as a point on the number line; extend number line diagrams to include negative numbers; understand signs of numbers in ordered pairs.

levels.4: Places all rational numbers (positive, negative, fractions, decimals) accurately on number lines and in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane; explains sign conventions.
levels.3: Correctly places positive and negative rational numbers on a number line and in the coordinate plane with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Places positive rational numbers correctly; errors placing negative fractions or decimals on the number line.
levels.1: Cannot reliably place rational numbers on a number line.

standards.description: Understand ordering and absolute value of rational numbers; interpret statements of inequality; distinguish comparisons of absolute value from statements about order.

levels.4: Orders rational numbers including negatives accurately; correctly uses and interprets absolute value; distinguishes absolute value from order in context.
levels.3: Correctly orders rational numbers and interprets absolute value with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Orders positive rational numbers correctly; errors ordering negatives or misinterprets absolute value.
levels.1: Cannot order rational numbers or apply absolute value correctly.

standards.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points in all four quadrants of the coordinate plane; find distances between points sharing a coordinate.

levels.4: Graphs points in all four quadrants accurately; calculates distances between points sharing a coordinate; applies to real-world problems involving perimeter or mapping.
levels.3: Correctly graphs points in all four quadrants and finds distances between same-coordinate points with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Graphs points in the first quadrant correctly; errors plotting in quadrants with negative values.
levels.1: Cannot graph points in all four quadrants or find coordinate-plane distances.

standards.description: Write and evaluate numerical expressions involving whole-number exponents.

levels.4: Writes and evaluates expressions with exponents fluently; distinguishes 2³ from 3² with explanation; applies in multi-step expressions.
levels.3: Correctly writes and evaluates numerical expressions with whole-number exponents with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Evaluates simple exponents correctly but confuses base and exponent, or errors with exponents greater than 3.
levels.1: Cannot write or evaluate expressions with exponents correctly.

standards.description: Write, read, and evaluate expressions with letters standing for numbers; identify parts of an expression using mathematical terms.

levels.4: Writes, reads, and evaluates algebraic expressions fluently; correctly names all parts (coefficient, term, factor, product, sum); substitutes values accurately.
levels.3: Correctly writes and evaluates algebraic expressions and identifies parts with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Evaluates expressions by substitution correctly but uses imprecise terminology or struggles to write expressions from verbal descriptions.
levels.1: Cannot correctly write or evaluate algebraic expressions.

standards.description: Apply properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

levels.4: Applies distributive, commutative, and associative properties fluently to simplify and generate equivalent expressions; explains each step.
levels.3: Correctly applies properties of operations to create equivalent expressions with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Applies the distributive property in simple cases; errors with factoring or combining like terms.
levels.1: Cannot apply properties of operations to generate equivalent expressions.

standards.description: Identify when two expressions are equivalent; recognize that equivalent expressions yield the same value regardless of the substitution.

levels.4: Identifies equivalence using multiple methods (substitution, simplification); proves equivalence and explains why; provides counterexamples for non-equivalent expressions.
levels.3: Correctly identifies equivalent expressions and verifies with substitution with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Identifies equivalence in simple cases; struggles to verify with varied substitution values.
levels.1: Cannot reliably identify equivalent expressions.

standards.description: Understand solving an equation or inequality as a process of determining which values make it true; use substitution to check solutions.

levels.4: Explains the solution process conceptually; verifies solutions by substitution; identifies the solution set for inequalities; applies to real-world constraints.
levels.3: Correctly identifies solutions by substitution for both equations and inequalities with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Substitutes to check equation solutions correctly; struggles with inequalities or solution sets.
levels.1: Cannot determine or verify solutions to equations or inequalities by substitution.

standards.description: Use variables to represent numbers and write expressions when solving real-world and mathematical problems; understand that a variable can represent an unknown number.

levels.4: Uses variables fluently in complex real-world contexts; writes expressions with multiple variables; explains what each variable represents.
levels.3: Correctly uses a variable to represent an unknown and writes a matching expression with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Writes expressions for simple situations; errors in multi-variable or multi-step problems.
levels.1: Cannot use variables to represent unknowns or write algebraic expressions.

standards.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems by writing and solving equations of the form x + p = q and px = q.

levels.4: Writes and solves both equation forms accurately; interprets the solution in context; checks the solution; extends to two-step problems.
levels.3: Correctly writes and solves x + p = q and px = q with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Solves one equation form correctly but not the other, or cannot write the equation from context.
levels.1: Cannot write or solve basic one-step equations.

standards.description: Write an inequality of the form x > c or x < c to represent a constraint; recognize that these have infinitely many solutions; represent solutions on a number line.

levels.4: Writes inequalities from context; graphs solution sets with open/closed circles correctly; explains that inequalities have infinite solutions; identifies boundary conditions.
levels.3: Correctly writes and graphs inequalities of the form x > c or x < c with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Writes inequalities correctly but makes errors graphing solution sets or confuses > and < symbols.
levels.1: Cannot write or graph simple inequalities.

standards.description: Find the area of right triangles, other triangles, special quadrilaterals, and polygons by composing or decomposing into rectangles and triangles.

levels.4: Finds area of all polygon types accurately; decomposes complex polygons into triangles and rectangles; explains strategy; applies to real-world contexts.
levels.3: Correctly finds area of triangles and special quadrilaterals by composing/decomposing with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Finds area of rectangles and right triangles correctly; errors with non-right triangles or composite figures.
levels.1: Cannot reliably find areas of triangles or composite polygons.

standards.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with unit cubes; apply the formulas V = l × w × h and V = B × h.

levels.4: Calculates volume with fractional edge lengths accurately; explains the unit cube model; applies both formulas; connects to fraction multiplication.
levels.3: Correctly calculates volume of right rectangular prisms with fractional edges using the formula with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Applies the volume formula with whole-number edges correctly; errors with fractional edge lengths.
levels.1: Cannot apply volume formulas, especially with fractional dimensions.

standards.description: Draw polygons in the coordinate plane given coordinates for the vertices; use coordinates to find side lengths.

levels.4: Draws polygons accurately in all four quadrants; finds all side lengths including those crossing axes; applies to perimeter/area calculations.
levels.3: Correctly draws polygons from coordinates and finds side lengths between same-axis points with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Draws polygons correctly in the first quadrant; errors with negative coordinates or finding distances.
levels.1: Cannot draw polygons in the coordinate plane or find coordinate-based side lengths.

standards.description: Represent three-dimensional figures using nets made of rectangles and triangles; use nets to find surface area.

levels.4: Draws correct nets for multiple 3D figures; calculates surface area accurately; connects net faces to the formula; solves real-world surface area problems.
levels.3: Correctly draws nets and calculates surface area for rectangular prisms and triangular prisms with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Identifies a correct net but makes errors calculating surface area or misidentifies face dimensions.
levels.1: Cannot draw nets or calculate surface area of 3D figures.

standards.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving area, surface area, and volume.

levels.4: Solves complex multi-step real-world problems involving area, surface area, and volume; selects the correct formula; labels units correctly.
levels.3: Correctly solves standard real-world area, surface area, and volume problems with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Solves area problems correctly; struggles with surface area or volume in applied contexts.
levels.1: Cannot solve real-world measurement problems involving area, surface area, or volume.

standards.description: Recognize a statistical question as one that anticipates variability in the data; understand that statistical questions produce data with variability.

levels.4: Distinguishes statistical from non-statistical questions; explains the concept of variability; gives original examples in context.
levels.3: Correctly identifies statistical questions and explains why they anticipate variability with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Identifies obvious statistical questions but struggles with borderline cases or cannot explain variability.
levels.1: Cannot distinguish statistical from non-statistical questions.

standards.description: Understand that a set of data collected to answer a statistical question has a distribution described by its center, spread, and overall shape.

levels.4: Accurately describes a data distribution using center, spread, and shape; connects these to the statistical question; uses formal vocabulary (symmetric, skewed, clustered).
levels.3: Correctly describes a distribution using center, spread, and overall shape with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Describes center or spread but not both; does not address shape or uses informal language only.
levels.1: Cannot describe a data distribution meaningfully.

standards.description: Recognize that a measure of center summarizes all values with a single number; a measure of variation describes how values vary.

levels.4: Explains the role of mean, median, and MAD with precision; chooses the appropriate measure for a given context; interprets each in context.
levels.3: Correctly calculates mean, median, and explains their role as measures of center and variation with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Calculates mean or median correctly but not both; limited understanding of variation.
levels.1: Cannot calculate or interpret measures of center or variation.

standards.description: Display numerical data in plots on a number line, including dot plots, histograms, and box plots.

levels.4: Creates accurate dot plots, histograms, and box plots; labels all components; chooses appropriate display for the data type.
levels.3: Correctly constructs at least two of the three plot types with ≤1 error.
levels.2: Creates a dot plot correctly; makes errors constructing histograms or box plots.
levels.1: Cannot correctly construct statistical plots.
